slides.headline: What 465,000 IRS Filings Reveal About Nonprofit Reserves
slides.subheadline: The sector is stronger than headlines suggest, and more divided

slides.label: Part 1: The Surprise
slides.headline: Most nonprofits hold real cushion
slides.accent_label: hold more than a year of operating reserves
slides.story: The common story says nonprofits live hand to mouth. The filings say otherwise. More than half the sector could run a full year on what they hold today.
slides.source: IRS 990 filings, 465,306 U.S. nonprofits with reserve data

slides.label: Part 2: The Divide
slides.headline: But the cushion is not shared evenly
slides.story: While half the sector holds a year of reserves, 42,473 organizations are operating on less than one month. Same sector, very different realities.

slides.label: Part 3: The Small Org Myth
slides.headline: Small nonprofits hold their own
slides.accent_label: of micro nonprofits run under 3 months of reserves, a lower rate than large organizations at 18.3%
slides.story: The assumption is that small means precarious. The data disagrees. Micro nonprofits manage their reserves as carefully as the giants, often more so.
slides.source: Daanaa analysis of IRS 990 data by revenue band

slides.label: Key Insight
slides.headline: Context beats assumptions
slides.accent_label: nonprofits operates on under 3 months of reserves
slides.story: You cannot tell which organizations run lean from their size, their name, or their website. Public filings tell the real story, and that story is free to explore.
